title:
💬  This is a list of product IDs for the FreeRDP client software, which allows users to remotely connect to Windows computers over RDP protocol. The product IDs are used by the FreeRDP server to identify and authenticate clients connecting to it. Some of the important product IDs include:

* FreeRDP\_ClientProductId - this is the unique identifier assigned to each instance of the FreeRDP client software installed on a computer. It is typically set during installation and cannot be changed later.
* FreeRDP\_EarlyCapabilityFlags - this flag indicates whether the client supports certain early capabilities required by the RDP protocol. If this flag is not set correctly, the connection may fail.
* FreeRDP\_NetworkAutoDetect - if this flag is set to true, the client will automatically detect the network configuration and use the appropriate settings for the connection. Otherwise, the user must manually configure the network settings.
* FreeRDP\_SupportAsymetricKeys - this flag indicates whether the client supports asymmetric encryption keys, such as RSA or ECC. If this flag is not set correctly, the connection may fail.
* FreeRDP\_SupportErrorInfoPdu - this flag indicates whether the client supports error information PDU messages, which can provide additional diagnostic information in case of errors during the connection process.
* FreeRDP\_SupportStatusInfoPdu - this flag indicates whether the client supports status information PDU messages, which can provide additional information about the state of the connection.
* FreeRDP\_SupportMonitorLayoutPdu - this flag indicates whether the client supports monitor layout PDU messages, which allow the client to request specific monitor configurations from the server.
* FreeRDP\_SupportGraphicsPipeline - this flag indicates whether the client supports graphics pipeline PDU messages, which allow the client to specify the rendering pipeline to be used for remote desktop sessions.
* FreeRDP\_SupportDynamicTimeZone - this flag indicates whether the client supports dynamic time zone synchronization, which allows the client's clock to be synchronized with the server's clock based on the current location.
* FreeRDP\_SupportHeartbeatPdu - this flag indicates whether the client supports heartbeat PDU messages, which are used to maintain the connection between the client and server.
* FreeRDP\_DesktopPhysicalWidth - this field specifies the physical width of the desktop screen in pixels.
* FreeRDP\_DesktopPhysicalHeight - this field specifies the physical height of the desktop screen in pixels.
* FreeRDP\_DesktopOrientation - this field specifies the orientation of the desktop screen, either portrait or landscape.
* FreeRDP\_DesktopScaleFactor - this field specifies the scale factor applied to the desktop screen, which determines how much larger or smaller the screen appears compared to its actual size.
* FreeRDP\_DeviceScaleFactor - this field specifies the scale factor applied to all devices connected to the system, including monitors, printers, and other peripherals.
* FreeRDP\_UseRdpSecurityLayer - this flag indicates whether the client uses the built-in security layer provided by the RDP protocol, or an alternative security mechanism.
* FreeRDP\_EncryptionMethods - this field specifies the encryption methods supported by the client, including AES, DES, RC4, and others.
* FreeRDP\_ExtEncryptionMethods - this field specifies any additional encryption methods supported by the client that are not included in the standard set of methods.
* FreeRDP\_EncryptionLevel - this field specifies the encryption level used by the client, ranging from low to high security.
* FreeRDP\_ServerRandom - this field contains a pointer to a buffer containing a random value generated by the server. This value is used to seed the client's random number generator.
* FreeRDP\_ServerRandomLength
